Venn

One adaptive plan for nutrition and training, with an AI coach that answers only from your own records.

Antonio Chicchón · MGT 409 AI Foundations for Managers · October 26, 2026

GitHub (public): https://github.com/antoniochicchonzapata25/venn
Runs locally: clone and follow the README. Demo login: demo / venn-demo-2026

The problem (from my own audit)

  • Two separate apps for food and workouts, two subscriptions, and no connection between them
  • Logging mistakes slip through: "70,000 calories" in one item
  • Generated workouts overrun: a 75-minute budget takes 100–120 minutes in practice
  • Injuries are hard to respect (my lower back, my knees)
  • No answer to "I train consistently but miss protein: what should I change?"

Personal observations from one experienced user, not a study.

What's new in Venn

  • Deterministic core is the source of truth: USDA food data, transparent targets, a workout generator, safety rules
  • Workouts never exceed your time (warm-up, rest and equipment changes included)
  • Limitations enforced in code: avoid or caution per body area, never diagnosed
  • Protein as a ±5% range, so you don't "fail" at 178 g of 180 g
  • AI coach across both domains, and every number it states is checked against your records
  • Body page: weight and measurement progress, plus a muscle-recovery map built from logged sets (an estimate, clearly labelled)

How the agents work

Router (keyword rules first) → Nutrition, Training or Progress agent → 8 read-only tools bound to the logged-in user → answer checks. gpt-6-luna only.

A real run (Progress Coach)

  1. Keyword router chose progress (no tokens)
  2. Luna asked for get_progress_metrics
  3. Then targets, top protein foods and the daily log
  4. Wrote "Observed" vs. "You could try", and noted the workouts are demo data
  5. Check: 5/5 numbers match records

Cost to run

avg of 6 live questions
~2.1k / 186input / output tokens per question measured
0 cache reads
$299/mofor 10,000 users projected
3 questions/day; 100 users ≈ $2.99
  • Logging, search, targets and workout generation use no AI: $0
  • Keyword router vs. model router, same 10 questions: the rules matched all 9 they routed and the model got 8/10, while saving ~85 tokens and ~1.6 s per question. Cheaper and not worse.
  • Caps: 6 model calls, 8 tool calls, 40 questions per day per user. Reference prices from the class slide.

Safety

  • Prompt injection in a food name: neutralised, flagged, and no extra tools (test + live run)
  • No cross-user access: no tool takes a user id; other users get 404 (tests)
  • Invented numbers are flagged ("Not found in your records")
  • Incompatible exercises flagged by the same rules as the generator
  • Overspending: per-run and daily caps; timeouts give no fake answer

Impact: the numbers (honestly)

  • 100% of generated workouts within the time limit, across 20–180-minute tests
  • 54/54 numbers in live AI answers matched stored records
  • 226 + 59 automated tests pass offline
  • ≈ $0.0003 per AI question; core tracking costs $0
  • Not yet measured: real users. There has been no pilot, so no time-saved claims. Next: a 2-week pilot with 5–10 two-app users

What's next

  • User pilot: logging minutes per day, workouts finished on time, days in the protein range
  • Smoothed weight trends in the Progress Coach; check recovery thresholds against users' soreness ratings; adapt workout length from planned-vs-actual history
  • Weekly coach summary (cached); prompt-cache-friendly prompts
  • Hosted version with per-user budgets
